articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Speedrunners Have Already Found New Ways to Break the Remake
articles.summary: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake.
articles.body:
From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake.

One of the best things about a new Zelda game is seeing just how quickly players can speed through it, but Nintendo's latest video game being a remake presents a unique situation. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has accumulated some of the most bizarre speedrunning strategies in its 28 years on the market, and in just a few days, the Nintendo Switch 2 remake looks like it will live up to that legacy.

Creative players started peeling back the layers of the new version of Link and Zelda's classic adventure just hours after it launched November 5. Even just moments into its life, they've discovered some seemingly useful (and hilarious) ways to break the game, with more almost certainly to be discovered in the weeks, months, and years ahead. Let's start with what might be the most common tactic under investigation so far: sending Link hurdling into the air at high speed.

Ocarina of Time Remake speedrunning has begun — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026

Ocarina of Time Remake speedrunning has begun

Ocarina of Time speedrunner Zfg1 seems to be one of the first to discover that the Switch 2 Zelda remake has interesting physics, which, if pushed far enough, can toss Link into the air like a firework. Even at first glance, you can probably guess how a safe landing from that height opens the door for players to get creative and skip portions of the game.

It seems relatively easy to replicate, too, with X/Twitter user @Vespher also sharing footage of them pulling off the same stunt in the same location. Other locations seem to be susceptible to Link's sudden weightlessness with some careful positioning, with a similar area highlighted by other players .

You might think that Link will only be able to fling himself skyward in extremely specific locations, but fear not, as there are other ways to send him for a ride. Another popular glitch making the rounds in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's first weekend in the public's hands only asks Hyrule's hero to stand in a chest. A few sudden movements (or even a well-placed bomb), and poof, ceiling.

Nocturne skip with a normalized setup and a buffered ocarina actor jump (ez mode) — Vespher (@Vespher) November 7, 2026

Nocturne skip with a normalized setup and a buffered ocarina actor jump (ez mode)

特定の宝箱の上でめっちゃ高く飛べるバグ ネタバレ注意 #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ — かえる (@k4erup) November 7, 2026

特定の宝箱の上でめっちゃ高く飛べるバグ ネタバレ注意 #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ

時のオカリナリメイク完全に理解した — せーら姫 (@sera18171) November 7, 2026

Like so many other frequently speedrunned games out there, Ocarina of Time players have picked it apart to find the fastest means of traversal. Whether it's walking backward, hopping, or rolling, there are plenty of different ways to get around Hyrule. Nintendo has done its best to make speed concerns a thing of the past in the Switch 2 remake thanks to Link's new sprint feature.

Did that stop fans from finding faster alternatives? Of course not.

In fact, hilariously, early speedrunning strats show that rolling, again, may have emerged victorious as the ultimate way to get to the final fight against Ganondorf as quickly as possible. There are two seemingly faster options so far: one involving hopping, and one without. The former, as outlined by YouTuber KnightPohtaytoe , requires players to target-hop forward into a roll and seems marginally faster than sprinting. The latter, shown by Reddit user Pomps8a , is a bit easier to get the hang of and simply asks Link to cancel his roll with a quick attack.

As this story is being written, the Zelda community has already found even more ways to skip sections of the game. One that started being shared around earlier today lets players climb walls by simply switching items.

デクの棒でジャンプ斬りする瞬間に他アイテムに切り替えることで高い足場にも届くバグが見つかった ほかの場所でも使えそう #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ — かえる (@k4erup) November 7, 2026

デクの棒でジャンプ斬りする瞬間に他アイテムに切り替えることで高い足場にも届くバグが見つかった ほかの場所でも使えそう #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ

All the speedrunning stats are still coming in , but so far, it looks like it will take the average player about 20 hours or so to beat The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. Content creator @MrGymnast86 is one speedrunner who started gunning for the fastest time out of the gate and managed to complete an Any% run in a little less than four-and-a-half hours . It's a time that will almost surely shrink as more methods are developed by the community.

The players looking to uncover sequence breaks – the ones who really want to get that game timer down just mere seconds if they can make it work – have found ways to allow Young Link to perform tasks only available to Adult Link and vice versa. As you might have guessed, the Ocarina of Time remake…doesn't really know how to tell the difference between the two if progress is made illegitimately. The results are almost impossible to describe, so you can see what some players have managed to capture below.

Using a glitch to get a really big jump in the remake, its now possible to get the silver gauntlets chest as adult, which is supposed to be gotten as child. The cutscene that plays after tries to fit adult link into child link model, which ends up looking like this. — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026

Using a glitch to get a really big jump in the remake, its now possible to get the silver gauntlets chest as adult, which is supposed to be gotten as child. The cutscene that plays after tries to fit adult link into child link model, which ends up looking like this.

This isn't possible with glitches yet, but if we can find a way to get into an adult only cutscene as child, we'll see this. — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026

This isn't possible with glitches yet, but if we can find a way to get into an adult only cutscene as child, we'll see this.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now for Switch 2. For more, you can see why IGN gave it a 9/10 review . You can also read about the developers who helped reimagine the Nintendo 64 classic for a modern audience.

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says He 'Experiments With AI' Just to Make Sure It's Not 'Good at Writing' Yet
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad."
articles.body:
Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad."

The Batman v. Superman and A Real Pain star explained why he finds the rapidly advancing and controversial technology unnerving – and how he deals with it – during a conversation with Variety . As he continues to plant his feet in Hollywood as a talent who can act, write, and direct, AI is something he's trying to keep his eye on in more ways than one.

"I have a paranoid answer for this," Eisenberg said when asked if he's nervous about the technology. "I’m totally paranoid. I sometimes experiment with AI to see whether it's good at writing. And it's still not.

"I’m paranoid, so I check and it still isn't. Thank God. I say, 'Write a scene like this.' I'm just testing it to make sure it's bad, and it's still bad. So I'm relieved, but, like, how far away is it from being good? How far are we from a kid putting on a pair of goggles and saying, 'I want to watch a movie about me where I rob a bank and then kiss the girl I’m in love with at school. Here are pictures of her, here are pictures of me' and then they press play? I'm paranoid about that."

While figures like George Lucas have supported AI in the past, there are plenty of entertainers who have spoken out against the technology as it has advanced in recent years. Goku's voice actor in Dragon Ball, Masako Nozawa, blasted those who had used AI to steal her voice for their own use . Nicolas Cage said he'll "probably not work with" Amazon again after he declined to sign its AI waiver. Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto said Nintendo would prefer to "go in a different direction" when speaking about the topic in September.

Eisenberg elaborated on his approach, saying that there are two saving graces: the power of the creative spirit and art that has stood the test of time. As AI development progresses to new and often intimidating places, these are the things that bring him some peace.

"Creative spirit will find ways to entertain and delight us and speak about things in a way that maybe computers won’t," he added. "The other thing I think about all the time, and [The Debut star Julianne Moore is] about to go to a play in New York, is that I do these Greek plays, which were written 2,500 years ago and we perform them the same way they were performed 2,500 years ago. If they’ve lasted that long, they’ll still be there.

"People want to be in the same room as other people, watching and listening to stories. It’s as old as cave people sitting by the campfire telling stories, and there will always be room for that. What I do worry about is whether we’ll still be able to make a living from it. I’m not 100% sure about that."

Eisenberg's next movie is The Debut , which is set to arrive December 11, 2026. In related news, the moviemaker recently reflected on how winning a Razzie for his role as Lex Luthor affected his career . In June, he talked about what it was like to turn down an opportunity to return as Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network sequel .

Photo by Zak Hussein/Variety via Getty Images.

articles.title: Nvidia Launches Investigation Into CEO Jensen Huang Following Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy
articles.summary: Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
articles.body:
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

The tech giant's board confirmed the news in a statement today, saying that it is looking into its concerns "in light of recent reporting" that Huang has "been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The update follows a late-October New York Times report , which stated the CEO had been unfaithful to his wife with an individual that U.S. intelligence believed to be involved in a Chinese spy plot.

The individual named in the report as having a relationship with Huang was Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. The CEO confirmed the affair in a letter sent to Nvidia staff (via BBC ).

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children,” he said. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

"Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation," he added. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.

"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."

Nvidia said that a committee of independent directors would oversee the effort with the assistance of outside independent counsel. The board said that it currently has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

The full statement follows: "The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.

"Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

Huang will remain Nvidia CEO as the investigation continues. The New York Times' report said that, as of last year, U.S. officials did not believe he was aware of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

articles.title: Petit Planet, aka HoYoverse's Take on Animal Crossing, Is Packed With Charm and Attention to Detail | IGN Preview
articles.summary: 2026 has been an incredibly crowded year for cozy life simulation games. Ironically, a genre that people usually turn to when they need a break from intense action games has started to wear me out. After playing Animal Crossing: New Horizons' latest update, Starsand Island; Pokémon Pokopia; Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream; and more, I found myself suffering from a different kind of fatigue. The fact that Petit Planet still managed to hook me despite all that says a lot about how it’s shaping up.
articles.body:
It will remind you a lot of Animal Crossing. This isn't a bad thing!

There are some nice touches that go beyond Animal Crossing that I appreciate.

The Switch 2 version won't be out until next year.

2026 has been an incredibly crowded year for cozy life simulation games. Ironically, a genre that people usually turn to when they need a break from intense action games has started to wear me out. After playing Animal Crossing: New Horizons' latest update, Starsand Island; Pokémon Pokopia; Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream; and more, I found myself suffering from a different kind of fatigue. The fact that Petit Planet still managed to hook me despite all that says a lot about how it’s shaping up.

As this genre continues to evolve in different directions, Petit Planet, developed by HoYoverse, aka the company behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail, is a game that follows closely in the footsteps of Animal Crossing. In particular, its inspiration from Animal Crossing: New Horizons, which introduced outdoor furniture placement and crafting to the series, is immediately apparent.

Petit Planet is built around the concept of living on your own uninhabited planet. After a simple character creation process, you sign up for a program offered by a company called Loomi Co., which lets you settle on an uninhabited planet. Guided by a dog named Mobai, you choose a planet with your preferred ecosystem and begin your new life. Mobai and his companions move in alongside you and help you get settled.

Mobai essentially fills the same role as Tom Nook in Animal Crossing. Petit Planet even makes a direct reference to its inspiration when he hands you a temporary housing kit, asking something along the lines of, "Wait, they made you take out a loan on your previous planet?" He reassures you that there's no such system here, which sounds wonderful—until you discover that upgrading your temporary home to a proper house still costs money. Sure, there's no loan, but that's only because you have to pay upfront! Tom Nook's influence is alive and well in this one.

The opening hours also feel remarkably similar to Animal Crossing. Shake a tree and fruit falls to the ground, with each planet having its own native fruit. You can decorate your tiny temporary home with furniture, change your character's clothes, catch bugs with a net, and fish with a rod. Fish and insects can be sold, used for cooking, or donated to a facility called the Eco House, which serves much the same purpose as the museum in Animal Crossing.

Even the little details are familiar. Nearby animals applaud or compliment you when you successfully catch a bug or fish, and newly discovered creatures come with amusing descriptions.

That said, despite using New Horizons as a clear foundation, Petit Planet has some interesting features that make it feel distinct. For example, in addition to fishing and bug catching, you can use a tong to collect shellfish and other creatures in shallow water. I particularly enjoyed trying to catch hermit crabs hiding beneath rocks, carefully timing my approach for the moment they emerged.

The way your planet develops is also quite different from anything in Animal Crossing. At the center of your planet stands a tree named Luca, which initially resembles the Town Tree seen in earlier Animal Crossing games. By completing various activities, you earn opportunities to water it, causing the tree to grow.

As the tree grows, the entire planet begins to change. At first, the changes are relatively small, such as flowers blooming nearby. Eventually, however, rivers and even oceans appear. Each stage of the tree's growth transforms the landscape, introducing new terrain and expanding the world around you. Growing this tree effectively serves as the game's main objective, giving you a reason to complete the various tasks scattered throughout your daily life.

The arrival of new animal residents is another area where Petit Planet takes a familiar idea and develops it further. As you progress, more animals gradually visit your planet, but rather than simply moving in, their introductions play out as little story events. You need to complete their individual story missions before they agree to settle down. The objectives themselves can be quite simple, such as catching a particular insect for someone, but these quests effectively serve as character introductions, giving each resident a little more personality before they become part of your community. Once the animals have moved in, they'll continue asking you for favors. Interacting with them gradually increases a relationship meter, almost as though Animal Crossing had borrowed a few mechanics from a dating sim.

Petit Planet - November 2026 Screenshots

Each character has their own specialties, likes, dislikes, and backstory. As your relationship grows, you learn more about them and receive rewards along the way. In that sense, Petit Planet gives you a clearer incentive to interact with your neighbors than Animal Crossing does, and seems determined to expand upon the idea of actually living alongside these characters.

Of course, there's a potential downside to this approach. If the game isn't careful, living with your neighbors could start to feel less like a natural relationship and more like completing a checklist to maximize their affection. That's something I'd like to examine more closely after spending additional time with the game. The inclusion of voice acting is just one indication of how much effort HoYoverse has put into Petit Planet's presentation. Personally, what impressed me most was the attention to detail in its animations.

For example, when your character stands up from a chair, they gently push it back into place with their hand. It might sound like an oddly specific thing to get excited about, but I can't recall seeing that animation in many other games. Likewise, when digging a hole with a shovel, your character places a foot on the top of the blade and presses down, just as someone would in real life. These small touches make everyday activities feel surprisingly convincing and help bring the planet to life.

The gestures you gradually unlock as you progress are equally well-animated, making the photo mode particularly enjoyable. At one point, I was lying on the beach when I noticed another character running around in the shallow water nearby. Watching this little scene unfold made me appreciate just how lively and charming the world of Petit Planet can be.

There's no denying that Petit Planet shares so many similarities with Animal Crossing that some players may accuse it of being too derivative. A system called Loomix Footprints, which rewards small everyday accomplishments with a special currency, is strongly reminiscent of Nook Miles. Likewise, learning how to craft new items by reading Create Cards feels almost identical to collecting DIY recipes.

And yet, Petit Planet remains immensely appealing. Part of that comes from the unique concept of living on a planet, but I suspect much of its appeal simply comes down to the exceptionally high quality of its execution. The furniture you can craft is consistently attractive, which only makes me want to spend more time decorating both my house and the surrounding landscape.

Little Planet and Petit Planet Screenshot Comparisons

I also had the opportunity to play a build with a considerable amount of progress already made. My character had access to a huge collection of furniture and clothing, allowing me to experiment freely with all sorts of decorative possibilities. Browsing through these items made me wonder whether Petit's greatest strength might actually be the sheer quantity and quality of its customization options. For someone like me, who spent countless hours decorating the interiors of houses and designing the landscape of my island in Animal Crossing, there's more than enough here to keep me occupied for a very long time.

There are plenty of items that naturally belong outdoors, too. Alongside familiar objects such as vending machines, which are also available in Animal Crossing, you'll find things like bus stops. With such a wide variety of furniture, it's easy to imagine creating entire residential neighborhoods, shopping streets, parks, and other themed areas.

Given the game's Chinese origins, I was also pleased to see a generous selection of East Asian-inspired furniture. I decided to turn a Chinese pond into a makeshift bathtub, transforming one of the rooms in my house into a Chinese style bathroom. Of course, not everyone enjoys designing an entire space from scratch. That's where the Blueprint system comes in handy. By placing the required furniture in designated positions, you can complete a predesigned facility or area. Better still, these creations aren't merely decorative. The residents of your planet actually make use of them.

During my play session, I followed a Blueprint to set up a projector, a popcorn machine, chairs, and more on the beach. Once everything was in place, an event was triggered in which the residents gathered to watch a movie together.

Seeing everyone happily enjoying a space I'd created gave me a sense of satisfaction that went beyond simply arranging furniture. This was actually one of the aspects of Animal Crossing that I had always found somewhat lacking.

I also got to experience Petit Planet during the winter season. Here, my planet had been transformed into a snowy wonderland. Snow covered the rooftops and trees, giving the familiar scenery an entirely different atmosphere. What impressed me most was that even some of the larger pieces of furniture I'd placed outdoors were covered in snow. Seasonal changes are nothing new to Animal Crossing, of course, but seeing player-placed furniture change its appearance to match the season felt like a particularly nice touch. Petit Planet reportedly features more than 1,000 free furniture and clothing items in total. Just imagining the amount of work involved in creating seasonal variations for even a portion of those items is enough to make my head spin.

Naturally, winter brings its own activities as well. Clearing away piles of snow rewards you with snowflakes, which can then be used to craft seasonal items such as the sled and a snowmonster. Eager to craft as many winter-themed decorations as possible, I started clearing snow wherever I could find it. To my surprise, one particular snow pile was hiding an incense burner underneath. Little discoveries like this help prevent what could otherwise be a repetitive chore from becoming monotonous. I was also surprised by the way you can throw snowballs. Rather than simply pressing a button to toss one, you can actually aim your throw using a targeting system reminiscent of a third-person shooter. Life simulation games tend to favor simple controls, but Petit Planet seems happy to borrow ideas from other genres. This approach makes its everyday activities feel more believable and interactive. And yes, you can also roll snowballs around to make them bigger, then stack two of them together to build a snowman. It seems that all the classic winter activities are accounted for.

Petit Planet also features seasonal events, and this time I got to experience one called the Season of Snowfall. takes place at a hot spring resort on another planet, where you meet the manager, Heyu, and help out with various tasks around the establishment. The gameplay mostly consists of straightforward errands, but the accompanying stories are so charming that I found myself eager to see what would happen next.

My favorite encounter involved a tiny rabbit named Maxwell, who happens to be a movie director. Apparently, he'd come to the area to scout locations for his next movie. He made a point of insisting that he had absolutely no intention of taking a dip in the hot springs himself. Yet a little while later, he returned with his teeth chattering from the cold. After I guided him to the hot springs, he happily jumped into the water wearing a swim ring. Apparently, as thanks for saving him from freezing to death, he's going to include my name in the special thanks section of his movie's credits.

Some players will undoubtedly feel that Petit Planet is simply too similar to Animal Crossing, and I can understand that criticism. However, it's worth remembering how Pokémon Pokopia borrowed numerous elements from Animal Crossing as well, while still managing to create an experience that felt fresh and distinctive.

HoYoverse itself has been through something similar before. Prior to the release of Genshin Impact, that game faced criticism for its resemblance to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. Once it launched, however, it quickly became clear that Genshin Impact had plenty of its own ideas and offered a distinctive experience.

I believe Petit Planet has every chance of following a similar path, drawing inspiration from Animal Crossing while developing an identity that players can appreciate on its own terms. In particular, its online features, which allow players to connect with one another, appear to be considerably more extensive than those in Animal Crossing. Unfortunately, I haven't had the chance to explore these systems thoroughly enough to offer a proper assessment just yet.

I also had the opportunity to spend some time with the recently announced Nintendo Switch 2 version. As it was still a work-in-progress build, I noticed a bit of frame rate stuttering, and there were noticeable visual differences compared to the PC version. Given how well cozy life simulation games are suited to the Nintendo Switch 2, I'm hoping the developers will be able to further polish this version ahead of its planned release in 2027 after the PC and mobile versions drop on December 4.

articles.summary: Ancestor's Weapons is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the snowy slopes of the Albaneve Summits to track down a mysterious and powerful weapon. If
articles.body:
Ancestor's Weapons is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the snowy slopes of the Albaneve Summits to track down a mysterious and powerful weapon. If you want to get your hands on Gunther's ancestor's weapon but you're not sure where to find it, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

How to Start the Ancestor's Weapon Quest

The Ancestor's Weapon quest is given to you by Gunther Galeforth, an NPC that you rescue during the Escaping From the Quarry quest in the Albaneve Summits. After securing Gunther Galeforth's soul, head back to your base and summon him. The Ancestor's Weapon quest is one of the first ones you get after speaking to Gunther at your base, so talk to him to hear the clues before setting off toward the lost treasure.

The weapon you're looking for is hidden in an abandoned crypt deep in the Albaneve Summits, very close to the place where you found Gunther Galeforth in the first place. You have to summon Gunther to get the quest, though, so you likely won't be near the Balefire Garrison "Windward" anymore. Therefore, your first step is to head back in that direction.

Start by fast traveling to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and soaring off the northeastern side. Drop down on the path, and start following it. You'll pass through an enshrouded area, the Gateway Outpost "Alba", the eventually find yourself in the Forge of Obsidia.

The Forge of Obsidia is actually the location of another quest, A Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith . Defeat enemies inside the main forge room until one of them drops the Bellows item. Tuck that away in your pack and use it to craft a Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith once you get back to your base!

For now, continue through the Forge by taking the doorway to the right and following that up a set of stairs. Turn left at the top of the stairs to get back outside again. Turn left as soon as you exit the building and continue following the path until you reach a dead-end.

Take a closer look at the cliff on your right to discover a cave entrance and a new path. Keep following that path through the cave to pop out the other side and take the path on the left to reach a high ledge.

Jump off the ledge and glide in a southwestern direction. The crypt is nestled in the side of the cliff on the other side of the ridge.

Now that you're at the crypt, the treasure is all but yours! You do have to find it down there, though. Start by defeating the spiders in your path and take the first path on the left.

Then turn right and follow the path about halfway up the hall before turning left to find a golden coffin that you can loot. Seize your spoils, head back out in to the crypt hall, and turn left.

Continue following the halls until you reach a room filled with spike traps. Sneak along the very edge of the room to avoid the traps and head through the door on the opposite side. Follow the halls to find yourself at another golden coffin that contains the weapon you were looking for: the Ancestral Star , a two-handed club. Collect it to complete the Ancestor's Weapons quest and earn yourself a new two-handed weapon!

articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Praises Human Creativity Over AI Prompts, Almost Announces New Bond
articles.summary: Denis Villeneuve Praises Human Creativity Over AI Prompts, Almost Announces New Bond
articles.body:
Denis Villeneuve has praised human creativity over AI prompts, and playfully stirred the pot over the increasing rumours and speculation surrounding the casting of the main character in his upcoming James Bond film.

Addressing the crowd at Saturday night's Art+Film fundraiser at the LACMA museum in Los Angeles where he was being honored for his contributions to cinema (thanks, THR ), the Dune: Part Three director took the opportunity to praise his heroes including Steven Spielberg and James Cameron, before speaking to the existential crisis currently being suffered by artists as a result of the rise of artificial intelligence.

"At the heart of every one of my films, there’s a question I need to answer," said Villeneuve. "The audience may see it or they may not, and that is fine. For me, each film is a statement to the unknown to try and find that answer. Perhaps those questions are more urgent now than ever."

"We are at the crossroad, asking what defines a human being and what human expression is worth? Every parent on Earth is a little worried about the world of our children will inherit. That question is at the heart of Dune: Part Three with Paul and Chani fighting to give their children a better world than the one they were given.”

The director went on to discuss the vital role that human creativity plays in the process of creating art.

“For a filmmaker today, it is very real," said Villeneuve. "I have a choice. I can create something with a prompt or I can go into the desert with actors, with a crew and go on a real adventure where I learn about life and become better at my craft. Those are two different things. Well, I know there’s producers in the room and they will say that one is more expensive than the other. More important than the result is the process. The process is how the human experience acquires its meaning. In this moment in time, it is more important than ever that human beings keep making art together. That is the heritage I want to give to my children.”

On a more lighthearted note, Villeneuve closed his speech by referencing the growing hype surrounding the casting of the next James Bond. Playing up to the headlines, Villeneuve said, "To express my gratitude with the blessing of my new friends at Amazon, I will reveal to you tonight who will be the next James Bond. The new James Bond is… and I will stop right now because Amy Pascal is about to have a heart attack. Thank you very much.”

Just last week it was reported that The Batman's Robert Pattinson had screen-tested for the role of 007 in the 26th James Bond film , and that Superman's Nicholas Hoult had also come into consideration. The two join Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O'Connor on the shortlist for the hotly-contested role , although nothing official has been confirmed by Amazon MGM Studios.

Casting for James Bond has been underway since spring, and since then rumours about who will take the role of the British super spy have been flying around from all angles like misfiring gadgets in Q Branch. Slow Horses' Jack Lowden would appear to be the frontrunner at least based on the feedback from fans, although former Bond Daniel Craig appears to be rooting for Josh O'Connor .

Meanwhile, Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three is set to arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026. Also arriving in theaters around that time are three Dune: Part Three popcorn buckets, including one with two sandworm mouths. Watch those teeth.

articles.title: U2's The Edge Apparently Wrote a Full Script for Elf 2 But Was Never Able to Bring It to Life
articles.summary: U2 guitarist The Edge apparently had such a good idea for Elf 2 that he went out of his way to write his own script.
articles.body:
U2 guitarist The Edge apparently had such a good idea for Elf 2 that he went out of his way to write his own script.

That's according to Elf actor and Dancing with the Stars legend Andy Richter, who spilled the beans about the musician's fondness for Christmas during an episode of The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast . It's a pairing no one ever saw coming but one that apparently still happened – or at least it almost happened.

Richter said the story of The Edge (real name: David Howell Evans) and his secret Elf 2 script comes from producer and frequent Will Ferrell collaborator Shauna Robertson. When exactly the elusive script would have been written is unclear.

"She was in Europe, and somebody reached out to her and said, 'The Edge from U2 has written a sequel to Elf, and he wants to talk to you about it.' It's the weirdest story, but apparently, it was fully written," Richter recalled. "Somewhere in the world, there is an Edge-penned Elf 2 out there, which I would love for that to make the light of day."

If you're unfamiliar with the guitarist or the group he's helped define for the last 50 years, U2 is the Irish rock band behind megahits like With Or Without You, I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For, Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where The Streets Have No Name, and more. He's a legendary guitar player behind a long list of instantly recognizable songs, and by comparison he's got little to no experience in the movie world.

A proper, fully written film script for Elf of all things marks a trip through mostly uncharted territory for The Edge. Unfortunately, it doesn't sound like his words will ever jump off the page and onto screens, and it's unclear if we'll ever get to read the supposed story for ourselves.

The Best Christmas Movies and TV Episodes of the 2000s

"It never happened," Richter continued. "It's just one of those things where she's like, 'All right, sure. I'll meet him,' you know? And then it just petered out and never, never happened."

Richter said he's on the side of Christmas fans who say "let it be." Directed by Jon Favreau and starring Ferrell, Elf is a holiday phenomenon which has yet to be matched in terms of sheer popularity, and that's probably why we may never see a sequel made. The Buddy the Elf star himself told IGN in 2016 that he never found the idea of following up the early 2000s classic with a full-on sequel.

"Now that that time has passed, I think that the movie has become so special that I think that people – and I think rightfully so – loathe to mess with it. Because we all can think of movies that have been tarnished by their sequels. This is so special and so perfect, and so beloved; why risk it?"

As far as what's been officially announced, Elf 2 is not in the works. While we wait to see if The Edge will change that, you can read what Ferrell had to say about the relationship he had with the late James Caan while filming the Christmas classic .

articles.title: Father Arrested After Leaving Sleeping 6-Year-Old Daughter in Line for Pokémon Cards
articles.summary: Father Arrested After Leaving Sleeping 6-Year-Old Daughter in Line for Pokémon Cards
articles.body:
A South Carolina man has been arrested and accused of leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target store overnight to hold his place in line for Pokémon cards, it has been reported.

According to the Washington Post , John-Michael Dooley, 35, had been waiting with his daughter outside the store this past Friday in Charleston's West Ashley district, where a throng of Pokémon fans had slowly gathered overnight in anticipation of a newly released set of the popular trading cards.

A news release from the Charleston Police Department states that officers arrived at the store around 2:30am after receiving reports of an unattended child. Witnesses at the scene told police that Dooley handed his daughter a blanket and a pillow sometime after 1am, before leaving her asleep in his spot in line. Wheen Dooley failed to return after an hour, these concerned witnesses were forced to contact the authorities.

Eventually Dooley returned to the store and was promptly arrested. In an interview with authorities, he admitted to police that he had gone home and left his young daughter unattended so that he could hold his spot in the line, according to the Charleston Police.

Dooley was then charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. Police said that the girl was unharmed and immediately placed into emergency protective custody.

This shocking act of Pokémon card-related parental neglect is in stark contrast to last week's news that the father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid had made a very moving plea to The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son. On his Instagram, Avery's father Christian Garcia said, "I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much." At the time of writing, there has been no official response from the Japanese company in regarding Garcia's request.

Pokémon Trading Cards, which is currently celebrating its 30th anniversary, was recently announced as one of this year's inductees into National Toy Hall of Fame , alongside Bingo, Care Bears, and the classic slide, and beating out nominees like Bop It!, mahjong, and Polly Pocket.

"Pokémon TCG’s widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," said curator Mirek Stolee. "The Pokémon TCG successfully adapted card game formulas established by its predecessors, making it more accessible and infusing it with the lovable Pokémon creatures."
